convoLines.text: "About the pantry run — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the east treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Maya owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"And... scene. Good talk."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
"Watch for this: It doesn't move. Speedbump, every time. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Still on the talking-to-strangers part. Anyway, I should move."
"It rewards action, not thought. You learn that fast when you're actually out there instead of theorizing about it."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about the big questions — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good — the big questions, settled. Feels better said out loud."
Someday this will be a story we tell laughing. I'm fast-forwarding to that part.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it?"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Nina has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that."
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Greta owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"Since Greta died... I keep expecting to see Greta at the fire. Stupid."
"Finally. I was wondering when you'd see my value."
"I sit apart to eat. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Still on the last time you laughed."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Nina shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "Make of that what you will."
"People here talk. What they say about you when you're not at the fire — that's the real answer to your question."
"And... scene. Good talk."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You said you're not good at the talking part either. For what it's worth — you're doing fine."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up? ...if that helps."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can I tell you something? I can't read, and I'm scared it matters now."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. Leo doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You saw it too, right? Cooking With Teeth. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You told me about the stolen laugh — someone tripping over nothing. Have you stolen any more since?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
A beat. Then, as if shaking something off:
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Cooking With Teeth. They just... took Leo. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"My part? I sharpen sticks down to nothing and stay ready."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
